issue_context.title: Net7 regression: Kestrel HttpRequestHeaders doesn't enumerate "Content-Length" unless there's another known header also present.
comments: This screams "perf cleverness", but I'll try to track down the exact code.

I'm immediately suspicious that there's [no `_bits`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/6c6361d2576da1800aeb8fa65cd2f0f94224edbd/src/Servers/Kestrel/Core/src/Internal/Http/HttpHeaders.Generated.cs#L4117) for content-length.

Edit: but there's at least some [special handling](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/6c6361d2576da1800aeb8fa65cd2f0f94224edbd/src/Servers/Kestrel/Core/src/Internal/Http/HttpHeaders.Generated.cs#L2586) for not including it in `_bits`.

@Tomius Can you tell us more about what impact this had?  Maybe it was just a fun puzzle for you, but it seems like a lot of work went into reducing the repro for us (thanks!) and I want to make sure that wasn't because it was causing some huge problem that would justify a backport.

Hello @amcasey,

Thanks a lot for looking into the issue and finding a fix.

I'm coverting a large codebase (~3000 csproj files) from net6.0 to net8.0, and during that migration I've encountered a test that was failing on net8.0 but it was passing on net6.0. 
It was testing a user implemented http header dictionary against the kestrel's implementation and was asserting that the two dictionaries behave the same way. So luckily the failing test pointed straight to the issue, and writing the repro was trivial.

As far as I can tell, we only rely on this behaviour in the test code but nowhere in production, so the impact is negligible for us.
